answer: Beacon-Threaded Neighbor Routing: each agent periodically broadcasts a beacon along its current task thread, and peers only accept work from agents whose beacon path traces back through distinct, previously active neighbors. A sybil cluster must keep every forged node continuously beaconing across real threads to stay reachable, costing sustained bandwidth and latency per fake identity rather than a one-time payment. Reachability decays if a node goes silent, so a lagoon of idle fakes is pruned from the routing graph and cannot rejoin without re-establishing threaded history.
